sights.w: The 1923 freight canal lined with stone warehouses and gas lamps — Otaru's postcard, best at dusk and during the February Snow Light Path.
The preserved Meiji–Taishō merchant street a short walk from the canal — glass workshops, music boxes, LeTAO and Kitakaro sweet shops.

sights.n: Otaru Music Box Museum (小樽オルゴール堂)
sights.w: The 1912 brick main hall at the foot of Sakaimachi, packed with thousands of music boxes — the Vancouver-gifted steam clock whistles out front. Free entry.

sights.n: Nikka Whisky Yoichi Distillery (ニッカウヰスキー余市蒸溜所)
sights.address: 7-6 Kurokawa-chō, Yoichi, Yoichi District, Hokkaido 046-0003, Japan
sights.w: Masataka Taketsuru's 1934 distillery, chosen because Yoichi most resembled Scotland — coal-fired pot stills, stone kilns and a tasting hall.

sights.n: Otaru City General Museum (小樽市総合博物館)
sights.w: Hokkaido's railway birthplace — steam locomotives in the old Temiya roundhouse, plus the canal-side annex in a former warehouse.
Japan's first Western-style fortress, the 1866 star fort where the Republic of Ezo made its last stand — a thousand cherry trees fill the moats in spring.
334 m peak at the tip of the peninsula: a three-minute ropeway to one of Japan's great night views, the city lights pinched between two bays.
The slope-side former foreign settlement — churches, the Old British Consulate, the Chinese Memorial Hall and the Old Public Hall of Hakodate Ward on stepped streets down to the harbour.

sights.n: Hakodate Orthodox Church (Holy Resurrection, ハリストス正教会)
sights.w: Japan's first Orthodox parish (consecrated 1860); the 1916 white church with green copper domes is an Important Cultural Property.
250-odd stalls across the street from Hakodate Station — squid you fish yourself, crab, uni and ikura donburi for breakfast.

sights.address: 144 Matsushiro, Matsumae, Matsumae District, Hokkaido 049-1511, Japan
sights.w: Japan's northernmost castle, seat of the only Edo-period domain on Hokkaido — its park is one of the island's great cherry-blossom spots, thousands of trees in 250 varieties.

sights.n: Upopoy — National Ainu Museum & Park (ウポポイ)
sights.address: 2-3 Wakakusa-chō, Shiraoi, Shiraoi District, Hokkaido 059-0902, Japan
sights.w: Japan's national centre for Ainu culture on Lake Poroto — the museum, a kotan of chise houses, dance, music and Ainu cooking.
'Hell Valley' above Hokkaido's most famous onsen town — a steaming crater of sulphur vents feeding nine kinds of spring water, boardwalk to Oyunuma.

sights.address: Tōyako Onsen, Tōyako, Abuta District, Hokkaido 049-5721, Japan
sights.w: Round caldera lake with an island at its heart and Mount Usu steaming on its shore — onsen town, summer fireworks every night.
Active volcano that last erupted in 2000 — the Usuzan Ropeway rises to crater rims and views over Lake Tōya and Shōwa-shinzan.
Japan's northernmost ice-free lake and one of its deepest and clearest — a caldera ringed by volcanoes an hour from Sapporo.
The zoo that reinvented Japanese zoos with behavioural exhibits — penguin parade in the snow, polar bears and seals in see-through tubes.

sights.address: Shirogane, Biei, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido 071-0235, Japan
sights.w: An accidental pond behind a volcanic-mudflow dam whose aluminium-rich water turns an unreal cobalt around drowned larches.

sights.address: Sōunkyō, Kamikawa, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido 078-1701, Japan
sights.w: Onsen town in a 100 m-cliffed gorge of the Ishikari River — Ginga and Ryūsei falls, and the Kurodake ropeway into Daisetsuzan.

sights.address: Asahidake Onsen, Higashikawa, Kamikawa District, Hokkaido 071-1472, Japan
sights.w: Hokkaido's highest peak (2,291 m) in Daisetsuzan National Park — a ropeway to steaming fumaroles and alpine tundra, Japan's first autumn colour.
